text: Write a program that bisects a failing computation, printing state at each stage so you can see where it goes wrong. Fill in the three blanks.
answer: System.out.println("after read : " + n)|System.out.println("after scale: " + n)|System.out.println("after clamp: " + n)
explanation: Verified: 7, 7000, then 5000. This is the cheapest debugging technique there is, and its value is not the printing but the *bisection* — you are halving the region where the bug can be, exactly as binary search halves a range. Chapter 32 makes that connection precise: ten well-chosen observations narrow a thousand-step program, and twenty narrow a million, because each one carries a bit of information.
